title: Royal Canin Medium Adult vs Josera Daily Menu Adult Ente

key_ingredients.name: Dried poultry protein, wheat, maize meal, wheat flour, maize, hydrolysed animal proteins, animal fat

alternative.product: Josera Daily Menu Adult Ente, 12.5 kg

key_ingredients.name: Wholegrain maize, rice, dried poultry protein, dried duck protein, beet fibre, poultry fat

summary: Both are complete dry foods for adult dogs on zooplus.de, and the Josera costs about 24% less per kg and about a fifth less per day for a 20 kg dog.
evidence: Both prices were read on zooplus.de product pages on 2026-11-06, with no discount label. Royal Canin Medium Adult 15 kg is EUR 65.99 (EUR 4.40/kg). Josera Daily Menu Adult Ente 12.5 kg is EUR 41.99 (EUR 3.36/kg). Both pages call the food an Alleinfuttermittel. Using each page's feeding table for a 20 kg dog, Royal Canin gives 235 g at low activity and 273 g at normal activity, and Josera gives 250 g at up to 1 hour of activity a day and 285 g at up to 3 hours. That works out at about EUR 1.03 to 1.20 a day against EUR 0.84 to 0.96 a day. The activity bands aren't defined the same way, so the daily figures are approximate. Per kg and per day figures are our calculation.
differences: Royal Canin has more protein and fat: 25% and 14% against 22% and 11%. Its recipe is made for medium dogs of 11 to 25 kg from 12 months, with a kibble of about 1 cm sized for them. The Josera is for adult dogs of all breeds, and its page gives no kibble size. The Josera is sold as gluten free, with maize and rice. The Royal Canin list has wheat and maize gluten. Neither food is grain free, and neither page states a kcal figure. The protein sources differ: the Josera has 10% dried duck protein plus poultry, and the Royal Canin has poultry, beef and pork proteins. Hundeo's summary says Öko-Test rated Royal Canin Medium Adult "sehr gut" in its November 2024 dry food test. We found no published grade for Josera Daily Menu. The same summary lists Josera as a brand in Stiftung Warentest 8/2025 but names no product or grade, so the Royal Canin has the better documented test record here. No trial compares these two foods.
why: The labels and feeding tables show the same everyday job at about a fifth less per day. The sources read don't show whether Royal Canin's extra protein and fat or its sized kibble change results for a healthy dog of this size.

title: Royal Canin Instinctive in Gelee vs Felix So gut wie es aussieht

brand.product: Royal Canin Instinctive in Gelee, 12 x 85 g

key_ingredients.name: Meat and animal by-products, vegetable protein extracts, minerals, vegetable by-products, oils and fats, yeasts

alternative.product: Felix So gut wie es aussieht in Gelee, Huhn, Rind, Thunfisch, Lachs, 44 x 85 g

key_ingredients.name: Chicken pouch: meat and animal by-products (14%, of which chicken 8%), vegetable protein extracts, fish and fish by-products, minerals, sugar

summary: Both are complete wet food for adult cats, sold as chunks in jelly in 85 g pouches, and the Felix costs about 72% less per kg and about 55% less per day for a 4 kg cat.
evidence: Both prices were read on zooplus.de product pages on 2026-11-06, with no discount label. Royal Canin Instinctive in Gelee 12 x 85 g is EUR 14.99 (EUR 14.70/kg). Felix So gut wie es aussieht, 44 x 85 g, Huhn, Rind, Thunfisch, Lachs, is EUR 15.29 (EUR 4.09/kg). The nearest Royal Canin pack in size, a 48 x 85 g Sparpaket at EUR 58.49, is EUR 14.34/kg, so the bigger pack barely changes the gap. Both pages call the food complete, for adult cats. For a 4 kg cat, the Royal Canin page gives 2½ pouches a day, and the Felix page gives up to 4 (up to 3 if neutered). That is about EUR 3.12 a day against up to EUR 1.39. Per kg and per day figures are our calculation.
differences: Royal Canin has more fat, 4.5% against 2.5%, with protein about the same at 11.9% and 11.5%, and slightly less moisture at 80% against 82%. Its feeding guide gives fewer pouches, so the saving per day is well below the saving per kg. Felix lists sugar and fish by-products. The Royal Canin jelly list has neither. The Felix pack mixes four flavours, 11 pouches of each. Neither page gives a kcal figure for these items. No taste or feeding test covers this pair.
why: The labels describe the same format for the same cat at similar protein, and the feeding guides still leave the Felix at under half the daily cost. The sources don't show whether the Royal Canin's extra fat or the Felix's sugar makes a difference to a healthy cat.
